message.content:
Java is a high‑level, class‑based, object‑oriented programming language that was originally developed by Sun Microsystems (now owned by Oracle) in the mid‑1990s. It’s designed to be:

- **Portable** – “write once, run anywhere” (WORA). Java programs compile to bytecode that runs on the Java Virtual Machine (JVM), which is available on virtually every platform.
- **Secure** – sandboxed execution, strong type checking, and built‑in security features.
- **Robust** – strong memory management (garbage collection), exception handling, and a rich standard library.
- **Multithreaded** – native support for concurrent programming.

Key features:

| Feature | Description |
|---------|-------------|
| **Syntax** | C‑style syntax (similar to C/C++/C#) but with automatic memory management. |
| **Object‑oriented** | Everything is an object (except primitives), with inheritance, encapsulation, and polymorphism. |
| **Standard Library** | Extensive APIs for collections, I/O, networking, concurrency, GUI (Swing, JavaFX), database access (JDBC), and more. |
| **JVM** | Executes bytecode; provides platform independence, just‑in‑time (JIT) compilation, and garbage collection. |
| **Community & Ecosystem** | Huge ecosystem of frameworks (Spring, Hibernate), tools (Maven, Gradle), IDEs (IntelliJ IDEA, Eclipse, NetBeans), and a massive developer community. |

Typical use cases include:

- Enterprise back‑end services (REST APIs, microservices)
- Android mobile apps (Java is one of the primary languages for Android development)
- Desktop applications (Swing, JavaFX)
- Big‑data processing (Apache Hadoop, Apache Spark)
- Embedded systems and IoT devices

Java has evolved through many versions (Java SE 8, 11, 17, 21, etc.), each adding new language features (e.g., lambda expressions, modules, records, sealed classes) and performance improvements.
